title: Install Entity Framework Core
description: Learn to create domain classes and understand the difference between domain classes and entities.

data.text: After installing the NuGet package for EF Core, it's time to create domain classes. We'll build a school application with `Student` and `Grade` classes.

data.title: Student and Grade Domain Classes
data.content: Creating domain classes for the school application

data.text: The terms "entities" and "domain classes" are often used interchangeably, but they are slightly different concepts:

rows: Contain core functionality and business rules
Tracked by EF Core for changes
May or may not be persisted

data.title: Making Domain Classes into Entities
data.text: To treat domain classes as entities, you need to include them as `DbSet<T>` properties in the `DbContext` class so that EF Core can track their status.

Entities in Entity Framework are mapped to corresponding tables in the database. EF Core keeps track of these entities so that it can perform database CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations automatically based on their object's status.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Domain classes contain business logic and rules
Entities are domain classes tracked by EF Core
Add DbSet<T> properties to DbContext to create entities
EF Core performs CRUD operations based on entity status
data.takeaway: Continue to the next lesson to learn about working with DbContext.
